transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Well, I've been having trouble going to the toilet. It's been getting harder to open my bowels, and I have to strain quite a bit.
When did you first notice this trouble?
It started about three weeks ago, I think. Before that I was fine.
Do you have any allergies or bad reactions to any medicines?
No, I don't have any allergies to medicines that I know of.
How much is this trouble with going to the toilet affecting your everyday life?
It's uncomfortable, the straining, maybe a 4 out of 10. And my lower tummy feels bloated. It's on my mind a fair bit.
What medicines, if any, are you taking regularly or have started or changed recently, and what dose if you know it?

I take co-codamol 30/500, two tablets four times a day — I started that about a month ago for my back pain. I also take apixaban 2.5 milligrams twice a day, and bisoprolol 2.5 milligrams once a day. And a calcium and vitamin D chewable tablet twice a day.
Whereabouts in your body do you feel this discomfort, and does it stay in one place or spread anywhere else?
The discomfort is mostly in my lower tummy, from the straining and the bloating. It stays there, it doesn't spread anywhere else.
Have you noticed anything at all that makes it easier or harder for you to go to the toilet?
I think I've been drinking less than I used to — only about three cups of tea a day — because I don't want to be getting up at night. I suppose that might be making it harder.
Apart from your back pain, is there anything else about your past health you think I should know?
Yes, I have osteoarthritis in my spine and my knees. And I've got an irregular heartbeat — atrial fibrillation, the doctor called it.
Besides the bloating in your lower tummy, is there anything else you've noticed that came along with your trouble going to the toilet?
No, nothing like that. No blood in my stools, nothing black, and I haven't been sick or vomiting.
What worries you most about your trouble going to the toilet?
I'd just like something to get things moving again, that's the main thing. But I do worry it could be something serious — you know, like bowel cancer. That's what's on my mind.
Have you ever had an operation or a stay in hospital for anything?
No, I haven't had any operations that I can recall, and I haven't been in hospital for anything.
Besides the co-codamol, apixaban, bisoprolol, and calcium and vitamin D you told me about, is there anything else you take — any other medicines, tablets, or supplements?
No, that's everything. Those are the only ones I take.
Is there anything else about your health that you haven't mentioned yet?
No, I don't think there's anything else. That's all I can think of.
Does this trouble with opening your bowels happen all the time, or does it come and go?
I go most days, really. It's just that it's harder to pass now than it used to be.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
